title: Recipe 04 — Multi-Agent Crew (three roles, one baton, one trace)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 04 opens by telling you not to reach for it: multi-agent helps on parallelizable work and hurts sequential reasoning. Crew is for roles that negotiate.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The smallest spec — three roles, one entry

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape, pick who starts
beats.cue: “entry: picks which role takes the first message — the ‘who goes first' problem is settled in the spec, not at runtime. And permissions are crew-wide, not per role.”

beats.label: Role 1 · the researcher
beats.cue: “List 3 concise risks of the topic. Then call Handoff(target="writer") and end your turn.” It hands off; it never writes the post.

beats.label: Role 2 · the writer
beats.cue: “Write a 4-sentence summary post. If you need a sanity check, use SendMessage(target="critic").” Handoff is one-way; SendMessage is request-reply.

beats.label: Role 3 · the critic
beats.cue: “Give a one-sentence direct answer. Be terse.” The peer that answers questions, never the one that ships.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the crew well-formedness passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Three roles, one entry, every role on the inherited sonnet — and look at each role's tools: empty.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target crew (3 roles, entry researcher); each role carries the inherited claude-sonnet-5 and "tools": []

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no key in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the daemon's stdin input gate

beats.label: Open the emitted orchestrator
beats.cue: “One file per role, plus this: three roles registered, one entry set. The baton passing is the runtime's job.”

beats.label: So where do Handoff and SendMessage come from?
beats.cue: “The recipe says you never declare them — here is the proof. The orchestrator builds both tools per role and pre-allows both patterns.”

verify.note: the installed crew-orchestrator imports createHandoffTool + createSendMessageA2ATool and pre-allows the Handoff / SendMessage patterns — which is why every role's declared tool list is empty

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A crew isn't a chat — the CLI names the two shapes it takes and exits 1.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1 — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "crew")`

beats.label: Boot the daemon with nothing to say
beats.cue: “The recipe says it in as many words: no input on stdin, no turn. It prints that and exits 2 — designed, not broken.”

verify.note: designed refusal — `[crew] no input on stdin`, exit 2; deps were installed by the --check beat

beats.label: Hand the crew a topic
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Researcher lists three risks, hands the baton to the writer, the writer pings the critic — three model calls minimum, four if it asks.”
beats.command: echo "Topic: rolling out vector-search to production" | bun live/dist/daemon.ts

verify.note: needs Anthropic credentials. The whole crew runs under one traceId and appends to a single sess_<hex>.jsonl; the recipe's debug command is `jq -c 'select(.kind == "crew_event")' "$SESSION"`

groups.title: One more thing · Per-role models — the cost lever

beats.label: Same crew, second spec
beats.cue: “Same three roles, same entry — now each role picks its own tier.”

beats.label: Haiku, opus, haiku
beats.cue: “Cheap structural extraction, high-quality synthesis, fast review.” The recipe's line: if every role runs the same opus model, the crew is just a chat with extra orchestration.

beats.label: Lint the mixed-tier crew
beats.cue: “Three models in one spec, still clean.”

beats.label: Compile it
beats.cue: “One file per role — so a per-role model is one literal per file.”

verify.note: plain compile (no --check: the shape is already proved above) — emits daemon, orchestrator and one agent file per role

beats.label: Read the tiers off the bundle
beats.cue: “Researcher on haiku, writer on opus, critic on haiku — the model-router only loads the adapters these two tiers need.”

verify.note: agent_researcher + agent_critic carry claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, agent_writer carries claude-opus-5
